body.en: The Digital SAT, taken on a computer, is section-adaptive: how you do on the first math module sets the difficulty of the second. The good news for math — a graphing calculator is built in and allowed throughout.

Math runs as two adaptive modules (about 44 questions in roughly 70 minutes). Questions are either multiple choice or student-produced responses (grid-ins). The on-screen Desmos graphing calculator is available on every question, and the math score is reported on the 200–800 scale.

blocks.note: Source: College Board — SAT Suite of Assessments Math Test Specification

body.en: Graph it in Desmos the moment you're stuck; plug in the answer choices or convenient numbers; and on grid-ins, don't round early — enter a fraction or a full decimal.

label.en: ⏱️ Digital SAT Math Pacing & Module Routing

body.en:
The Digital SAT Math section consists of two 35-minute modules of 22 questions each (~95 seconds per question):

  • Module 1 (Routing): A broad mix of easy, medium, and hard questions. High accuracy here routes you to the harder Module 2, unlocking scores up to 800.
  • Module 2 (Scoring): Your difficulty tier is locked. Scoring well on the harder module ensures a top percentile score. If routed to the easier module, maximum scores are capped (~600).
  • Pacing Rule: Never spend more than 2 minutes on a single question in Module 1. Flag it, make an educated guess, and move forward to secure all straightforward points.

• Over-calculating with Desmos: While Desmos is accessible throughout, entering complex equations for basic mental algebra burns valuable time. Use algebraic shortcuts when obvious.
  • Grid-In Formatting Errors: Student-Produced Responses accept up to 5 characters (including negative sign - and decimal . or fraction slash /). Never enter mixed numbers like 3 1/2 (read as 31/2); enter 7/2 or 3.5. Never round repeating decimals prematurely: 2/3 must be entered as 2/3, .6666, or .6667 (never .66 or .67).
  • Leaving Questions Blank: There is zero penalty for incorrect guesses. Always fill every single bubble or grid-in before the timer expires.
  • Calculator Angle Mode: For trigonometry questions, check whether the angle is given in degrees or radians. Desmos defaults to radians; switch to degree mode in the wrench settings when working with degree values.

1. 1. Always answer what is asked: The SAT frequently solves for \(2x\), \(x+y\), or \(b\), rather than \(x\). Highlight the target quantity.
  2. 2. Use regression for constant fitting: Type points into a Desmos table and use y1 ~ mx1 + b or y1 ~ a(x1-h)^2 + k to solve unknown parameters instantaneously.
  3. 3. Backsolve from the choices: On single-variable equations with complicated structures, substitute choice B or C to eliminate options rapidly.
  4. 4. Mind the reference sheet: Geometry formulas (spheres, cones, pyramids, special right triangles) are always available via the in-app reference icon — never guess a standard volume formula.
